page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r6.3xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring 12 vCPUs across 6 physical cores with Hyper-Threading, based on the Intel Xeon Platinum 8269CY processor operating at 2.5 GHz. It includes 96 GB of RAM, supplying an 8 GB per vCPU allocation ratio suitable for memory-intensive enterprise tasks. The instance utilizes x86_64 architecture under a KVM hypervisor and supports vector instructions including AVX-512.

Benchmark evaluations indicate average multi-threaded processing power alongside weak single-core metrics. Stress-ng multi-core testing achieves a score of 10,482.47, whereas single-core performance registers in the lower 25th percentile. Geekbench 6 testing produces a single-core score of 1,169.0 and a multi-core score of 5,949.0. Potentially uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 71.39 GB/sec, while uncached write bandwidth registers at 43.14 GB/sec.

The server provides a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps and does not include bundled local SSD storage or GPU acceleration. In database workload benchmarks, the server handles 10.13 million Redis SET operations per second and registers a PassMark database score of 4,226.24.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU density, the ecs.r6.3xlarge offers efficient resource utilization for in-memory database engines, caching layers, and memory-bound enterprise applications without requiring excess CPU core allocation. Primary hardware tradeoffs include lower single-core execution speed and total reliance on network-attached storage.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r6.3xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server instance configured with 12 vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon Platinum 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz and 96 GB of RAM. Built on x86_64 architecture with KVM virtualization, it provides an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. The system includes support for AVX-512 extensions, a 4 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and no local storage. In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates average multi-core CPU and memory bandwidth performance, recording a Geekbench multi-core score of 5,949.0 and handling over 10 million Redis SET operations per second. Single-threaded performance falls into the lower percentile spectrum. The ecs.r6.3xlarge instance provides an economical balance for memory-heavy enterprise deployments, relational database clusters, and in-memory key-value stores where high memory density is prioritized over peak single-core execution clock speeds.
